title: Intelligent runbook triggering and pager signal decontamination
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our paging signal is too noisy during short-lived region skews and autoscaler churn, causing on-call fatigue and slow triage. Goal: Reduce noise while preserving high-fidelity SLO breach alerts and enable automated, context-rich runbook actions that can be executed safely (or suggested) by the on-call user interface and via chatops. Scope: 1) Add a deduplication and signal-scoring layer that suppresses repeated or low-impact pages while surfacing correlated incidents. 2) Integrate circuit-breaker state into alerting so runbooks and pages reflect degraded modes (eg. circuit: open, shedding: true). 3) Wire deterministic runbook automation hooks to incidents: auto-collect context, propose next steps, and optionally execute safe mitigation primitives (eg. route shift, scale-down/scale-up throttle, temporary throttling by customer tier). 4) Tie dynamic alert thresholds to SLO burn rates and region-aware failover status so alert severity follows the customer-impact vector. 5) Provide an audit trail and rollback for any automated actions.
updates: 2025-02-20: Spike complete for dedupe algorithm; evaluated three approaches — time-window hashing, request-context fingerprinting, and causal grouping. Chosen: causal grouping + sliding window to preserve correlated incidents across multi-region RPC failures.
2025-02-25: Prototype wire-up of circuit-breaker telemetry into Alert Engine v2. Circuit state (closed/half-open/open) is now emitted to event metadata and available to runbook templates.

2025-02-28: Implemented early version of runbook templating. Templates can ingest event metadata (model, region, route, SLO burn rate) and render a prioritized action list. Manual review required before automated execution for high-impact actions.
2025-03-01: Synthetic check added to validate dedupe does not drop P0 signals. Ran chaos injection against staging — dedupe suppressed 72% of redundant pages while preserving all seeded SLO breaches.
2025-03-03: Building chatops integration (Slack / Teams) to allow one-click runbook step approvals and safe-parameter prompts. ETA for MVP: 2025-03-12.
Next: Add telemetry for false suppression and an override flow for on-call to re-open suppressed incidents; finalize escalation matrix mapping to new severity labels.
comments: PM review (Ravi Desai): Love the SLO-linked thresholds. Please ensure runbook suggestions are explicit about customer impact and safe-fail behaviors. Link to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Noise+Reduction+and+Runbook+Automation

Design feedback (Marina Gomez): Add a compact UI card for runbook suggestions that includes: expected change, risk, rollback knob, and telemetry snapshot. See mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UiMockup
Infra review (Ethan Kim): Circuit state propagation looks good; ensure low-cardinality tags to avoid high cardinality in metrics. Suggested tag set: region, route_group, circuit_state, severity.
SRE run (on-call): After staging chaos, noted a false-suppression when two different downstream errors share a shard id. Follow-up subtask created to widen grouping keys.

GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alert-engine/pull/457 — includes dedupe core and new alert metadata schema. Waiting on: unit tests for grouping edge cases and integration test for multi-region event ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Deduplication reduces redundant pages by >=50% for non-SLO-breach alerts in staging chaos test suite
All P0/P1 SLO breach signals are never suppressed; suppression metrics and examples are stored for post-incident review
Runbook templates can be rendered with event metadata and provide explicit safe-execute flags
Chatops one-click execution triggers a documented audit log and a reversible mitigation action
Circuit-breaker state appears in incident context and influences severity mapping and suggested mitigations
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive suppression could hide real customer-impact incidents. Mitigation: whitelist SLO-breach signals and add a conservative fail-open policy that favors paging under uncertainty.

Risk: Automated mitigations might cause cascading effects across regions. Mitigation: require manual approval for cross-region actions; sandboxed execution for canary scope and automatic rollback on metric regressions.
Risk: High cardinality from added metadata. Mitigation: enforce a limited tag set and apply cardinality bucketing for unbounded fields.
Risk: On-call confusion with new severity labels. Mitigation: update runbook training, provide migration notes, and a 2-week parallel mode where both old and new labels are visible in dashboards.
